headline: Every major still under its 200-day line while the crowd sits in fear
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it settles everything else. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day moving averages, and none carry a golden cross. That is seven for seven. When the entire board sits under its long-term trendline, you are not looking at isolated weakness in one coin, you are looking at a market that as a whole has not repaired its longer trend. BTC is 48.1% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is 60.1% off its own high, and ADA is a striking 82.8% below its year high. This is a market working from underneath, not one pulling back from strength.

Momentum tells a more mixed story than trend does, and that gap matters. BTC's RSI sits at 52.7, ETH at 58.1, both comfortably in neutral-to-firm territory, and BTC is up 1.33% and ETH up 0.73% on the day. Yet both have MACD below signal, and neither has reclaimed its 200-day. That is a market recovering some momentum while the trend itself stays negative, worth naming as a lag rather than a reversal. BNB and DOGE show MACD above signal, a small tell that their short-term momentum has turned up even as they too sit below their 200-day lines. SOL and ADA, by contrast, have RSI near 45-50 and MACD still under signal, so their bounce (0.9% and 2.27% on the day respectively) looks more tentative.

Positioning adds texture. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0065% per 8 hours (7.1% annualized), a modest cost for longs, not a crowded, expensive trade. Open interest of just over $2.0B alongside a long/short ratio of 1.41 says leveraged positioning leans long but isn't stretched. ETH funding is almost flat at 0.1% annualized with a long/short ratio of 1.54, similarly unspectacular. SOL stands out with funding at negative 8.0% annualized, meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their position there, an unusual setup given SOL's long/short ratio of 2.74 (heavily long by account count) coexists with negative funding, a genuine divergence between who's positioned and who's paying. Liquidations over the past day were fairly balanced across assets, with BTC longs taking slightly more damage ($6.87M) than shorts ($5.12M), consistent with a market that dipped and squeezed both sides rather than one clean wipeout.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. BTC spot ETFs posted a positive $32.1M on 29 Jul 2026, but the five-session net is negative $494.4M, and same_direction_days of 1 means that single positive day breaks, rather than confirms, a losing streak. ETH ETFs were negative on the day (-$32.9M) and negative over five sessions (-$56.2M) too, so the traditional-finance bid has been soft on both majors this week even with today's single green tick in BTC. Whale flows lean the same way: the last 24 hours show a net $112.7M moving onto exchanges, led by a $193.7M BTC deposit to Kraken, partially offset by an $81.0M BTC withdrawal from Binance. Zoom out to the weekly net figures however, and the picture flips around: after three days of outflow-heavy or mixed prints, the most recent reading was +$1.163B net off exchanges, so today's single-day move onto exchanges sits inside a choppy, not one-directional, week. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, has actually shrunk 1.62% over 30 days to $304.5B, a modest fade rather than a buildup.

Sentiment is the clean foil to all of this. The Fear & Greed gauge reads 28, squarely in Fear, and sits mid-range within its own 30-day band of 11 to 33, meaning today's reading isn't even the extreme end of the recent mood. The crowd is anxious, yet BTC and ETH are green on the day with RSI recovering into the 50s and 8-of-30 funding levels cheap rather than crowded. Fear in the gauge and calm-to-firming momentum in the tape do not agree, and that disagreement, rather than either reading alone, is today's more interesting signal.

What's worth watching from here: whether BTC or ETH can close back above their 200-day lines, since right now momentum is trying to recover under a trend that hasn't turned; whether the ETF five-session net flips positive on both BTC and ETH rather than showing one green day inside a red week; and whether SOL's negative funding alongside its high long/short ratio resolves toward one side, since that mismatch between who's paying and who's positioned rarely sits still for long.
